messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 51-year-old man comes to the physician because of severe pain while urinating for 4 days. He has also had to urinate more often than usual. Three weeks ago, he underwent surgery for an incarcerated hernia. While recovering, he developed septic shock and was treated in the intensive care unit. He was discharged 6 days ago. He has a history of hypertension. Current medications include amlodipine and oxycodone. He appears anxious. His temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), pulse is 96/min, and blood pressure is 122/80 mm Hg. Examination shows tenderness to palpation in the suprapubic area; no guarding is present. There is a well-healed surgical scar in the right inguinal region. There is no costovertebral angle tenderness. Urinalysis shows:
Blood 1+
Protein 1+
Nitrite positive
Leukocyte esterase positive
RBC 1–2/hpf
WBC 20–25/hpf
Which of the following would have most likely prevented this complication?"

Options:
A. Intermittent catheterization
B. Prophylactic oral ciprofloxacin
C. Topical mupirocin application
D. Use of a hydrophilic catheter
E. Screening for bacteriuria

Correct answer: A. Intermittent catheterization

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "The question tests prevention of catheter-associated urinary tract infection after ICU hospitalization; the patient's anxiety is incidental and no psychiatric or DSM-5 knowledge is involved."}
